chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Day of Meeting is the Day when the people of Heaven and the people of Earth meet. The Day of Calling is the Day when the people of the Fire call to the people of Paradise: 'Pour upon us from the water or from what Allah has granted you.' The Day of Undervaluing is the Day when the people of Paradise undervalue the people of the Fire. The Day of Brokenheartedness is the Day when Death is brought and slaughtered.
ai.seo_question: What are the four specific days of the afterlife mentioned in Shia hadith regarding the meeting of people and the end of death?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents these four days as distinct eschatological phases, moving from the initial convergence of realms to the final, absolute end of mortality. The 'Day of Brokenheartedness' (Yawm al-Hasarah) is particularly significant in Shia tradition as it marks the definitive end of death's reign, fulfilling the divine promise that death itself shall be slain. This progression underscores the transition from temporary worldly trials to eternal, unchanging states of bliss or regret.
